facebook.long_form:
The American League Championship Series comes down to one game.

Tied 2-2, the Tampa Bay Rays and Cleveland Guardians face off in a decisive Game 5 today at Progressive Field — 5 PM ET on TBS/HBO Max. The winner earns a trip to the 2026 World Series to face the Milwaukee Brewers. The loser goes home.

On the mound: Drew Rasmussen (1-0, 1.29 ERA this postseason) for Tampa Bay faces Parker Messick (0-2, 3.09 ERA) for Cleveland. Rasmussen has been Tampa's most dominant arm all October, including a stellar eight-inning performance in the Division Series opener. Messick is throwing a career-high 198 innings between the regular season and playoffs, and hasn't been as sharp in his postseason outings as his regular-season résumé would suggest.

The offensive story heading in: Tampa Bay's big three — Junior Caminero, Yandy Díaz, and Jonathan Aranda — were a combined 5-for-34 with just one RBI entering Game 4. Then Caminero ripped a 110.7 mph laser to break a 1-1 tie in the sixth inning. The Rays won 7-3. Now the question is: was that a breakthrough, or just one big night?

In ALCS history, the team that wins Game 5 to take a 3-2 series lead advances to the World Series about 66.7% of the time. The stakes are exactly that high today.

stories.title: Jake Bauers NLCS MVP — The Retirement Almost Nobody Knew About
stories.angle: Bauers was ready to retire before the 2026 season. His wife's pregnancy convinced him to keep playing for the health insurance. He stayed. He hit a go-ahead HR in NLCS Game 3, drove a two-run ground-rule double in Game 4 to fuel the sweep, collected 6 RBI to earn NLCS MVP. No Brewer had ever won the award before. The story writes itself.

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text:
Jake Bauers was ready to retire before this season.

His wife was pregnant. He stayed for the health insurance.

He just won NLCS MVP with 6 RBI and a series-clinching double. No Brewer had ever won that award.

Life comes at you fast. ⚾

#MILBrew #MLB

facebook.long_form:
Before this season, Jake Bauers was ready to walk away from baseball.

He and his wife were expecting their first child. He'd had stretches of decent play and stretches of struggle, and the grind of professional baseball was wearing on him. Retirement was the plan — until the baby changed everything. He needed health insurance. He kept playing.

Then October happened.

Bauers hit a go-ahead two-run home run in the seventh inning of NLCS Game 3 to give Milwaukee the lead for good. In Game 4, he ripped a two-run ground-rule double in the fourth inning to help fuel the Brewers' sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers. He hit in all four games. He drove in six runs — the most on the team. He became the first Brewer in history to win the League Championship Series MVP Award.

No Milwaukee player had ever won that trophy in the franchise's 58-year history. Bauers did it while batting .286 for the series (4-for-14), making clutch plays at the moments that mattered most, against one of the most expensive and decorated rosters in baseball.

"We knew we were going to win," Bauers said after the series-clinching Game 4 victory at Dodger Stadium.

Sometimes a pregnant wife keeps you from retiring. Sometimes that leads to a World Series.
facebook.image_caption: Jake Bauers was ready to retire this year. His wife's pregnancy convinced him to stay for the health insurance. He just won NLCS MVP — the first Brewer ever to earn that trophy. 6 RBI, 4 for 14, a go-ahead homer, a series-clinching double. Life comes at you fast.

article.headline: Almost Retired. Now an NLCS MVP. The Remarkable Story of Jake Bauers.

stories.angle: Jacob Misiorowski starts Game 1 on Oct 23 at American Family Field (8 PM ET, FOX). facebook.long_form:
Jacob Misiorowski will start World Series Game 1.

That much is confirmed. The 22-year-old right-hander — who led the Brewers rotation with a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts during the regular season — will take the mound at American Family Field on Friday, October 23, with the benefit of 12 days between starts.

That rest matters. Misiorowski's NLCS outings were effective but short: he needed 94 pitches to get through 3⅔ innings in Game 1, and the Brewers' bullpen (DL Hall, Trevor Megill, and company) picked up the remainder. With nearly two weeks to reset, the mechanical issues that produced those short outings may be behind him. A fresh version of Misiorowski — throwing triple digits with movement — is one of the most difficult matchups in baseball.

Game 1 is Friday, October 23, at 8 PM Eastern time on FOX. Logan Henderson is expected to start Game 2 on Saturday. Milwaukee hosts the first two games before the series shifts to the American League park for Games 3-5.

The Brewers were 103-59 in the regular season and earned home-field advantage. They've waited 44 years for this. They're ready to use every advantage they have.

stories.title: Caminero Wakes Up — 110.7 MPH Launch Powers Rays' Game 4 Win
stories.angle: Before Game 4, Caminero/Díaz/Aranda were a combined 5-for-34 with 1 RBI in the ALCS. Then Game 4: Caminero ripped a 110.7 mph laser in the 6th inning to break a 1-1 tie. Rays won 7-3. His bat waking up changes Tampa's World Series hopes. Now he's the key to Game 5 and beyond.

Before Game 4: Caminero, Díaz, and Aranda were a combined 5-for-34 with 1 RBI in the ALCS.

Then Caminero hit a 110.7 mph laser in the 6th. Rays win 7-3. Series tied 2-2.

That's why he's Tampa Bay's most dangerous bat. #RaysUp #MLB

facebook.long_form:
Through three ALCS games, Tampa Bay's most dangerous hitters had gone quiet.

Junior Caminero, Yandy Díaz, and Jonathan Aranda — three of the most feared bats in the Rays lineup — were a combined 5-for-34 with just one RBI as the Guardians took a 2-1 series lead. Tampa's season was in danger of ending not with a bang but with a quiet series of groundouts and strikeouts.

Then came Saturday's Game 4 at Progressive Field.

Caminero stepped to the plate in the sixth inning with the game tied 1-1 and did what he does at his best: he hit the ball harder than most humans can swing a bat. Exit velocity: 110.7 mph, which according to Statcast analysts was the defining hit of the game. The ball didn't just leave the park — it sent a message. Final score: Rays 7, Guardians 3. Series tied, 2-2.

For Tampa Bay, Caminero's breakthrough couldn't have come at a better time. He's the Rays' most dangerous power source, a player analysts have called the key to the pennant if Tampa is going to advance. Now, heading into Game 5 today, the question is whether Saturday was a turning point or a single hot night.

Given what Caminero is capable of — and what he showed Saturday — the Guardians have to respect that lineup in a way they haven't had to this series.

The 2026 World Series is five days away.

Milwaukee Brewers vs. the American League champion (determined tonight in ALCS Game 5 between Tampa Bay and Cleveland). Every game on FOX. Milwaukee hosting Games 1 and 2. The World Series could last until Halloween.

Here's everything you need to know:

Game 1: Friday, October 23 — Milwaukee (8 PM ET, FOX)
Game 2: Saturday, October 24 — Milwaukee (8 PM ET, FOX)
Game 3: Monday, October 26 — AL Park (8 PM ET, FOX)
Game 4: Tuesday, October 27 — AL Park (8 PM ET, FOX)
Game 5: Wednesday, October 28 — AL Park (8 PM ET, FOX, if needed)
Game 6: Friday, October 30 — Milwaukee (8 PM ET, FOX, if needed)
Game 7: Saturday, October 31 — Milwaukee (8 PM ET, FOX, if needed)

📺 HOW TO WATCH
All games on FOX (English). FOX Deportes and Univision carry Game 1 in Spanish. Stream on FOX One or FOXSports.com with a TV provider.

🏆 THE STORY
Milwaukee's last World Series was 1982. That's 44 years. The city hasn't seen anything like this since before many of its current players were born. The Brewers were 103-59 this season, earned home-field advantage, swept the Dodgers in the NLCS behind Jake Bauers' NLCS MVP performance, and now get 12 days of rest to prepare Jacob Misiorowski for Game 1.

The wait is over. The World Series starts Friday.
